messages:
Ashwin K: Quick heads-up — I ran the monthly storage burn numbers and traces are the big driver. Proposal: move non-prod (dev/staging) traces to 7d hot TTL then auto-archive to cold for 90d; prod stays hot for 30d then cold for 180d. Thoughts?

Maya L: Do we have hard numbers on query cost from cold vs keeping warm?

Ashwin K: infra-bot posted an initial delta earlier — keeping prod warm an extra 30d is ~0.9TB/mo extra, cost ~ $2.6k/mo. Cold reads are ~3x more expensive per query.

Tom B: For customer-facing debugging (SLO regressions) we need fast access to traces for the 30d window. After that, need to balance support workflows vs cost. Can we route searches differently by tenant? e.g., premium tenants always get 90d warm.

Maya L: Tenant-aware routing sounds right but adds index complexity. We already have a "tier" label in spans. Could add a routing rule that pins index shards to hot cluster based on label.

SRE Sam: Concern: rollouts UX. If we suddenly move a service's env to cold, support will hit more opaque errors while rehydrating. We need a clear deprecation policy + bump in console indicating query latency/backfill status.

Tom B: Agree. Add a UI indicator in traces that says "archived / cold — rehydrate in X mins" and show approximate cost of rehydrate. That helps on-call decide.

Ashwin K: Implementation note: OpenTelemetry exporter already tags resource.env and service.name. We could add resource.attributes["billing.tier"] and then use that in retention routing. Example config idea:

```yaml
exporters:
  otlp/http:
    endpoint: \"https://collector.redwood.internal:4318\"
    headers:
      x-tenant-tier: \"${BILLING_TIER}\"
processors:
  batch:
    timeout: 200ms
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [batch, attributes]
      exporters: [otlp/http]
```

Maya L: If we use billing.tier we should validate existing SDKs don't overwrite. Also need migration plan for historical spans with no tier label.

infra-bot: cost-alert-bot:monthly_summary: Stored traces this billing month: 13.1 TB. Hot tier: 9.4 TB, Cold tier: 3.7 TB. Estimated monthly savings if non-prod -> 7d hot + cold: $18,200 (approx).

SRE Sam: For queries, can we have a lightweight index that keeps trace ids and timestamps in hot so we can redirect to cold storage fast and avoid full rehydration? That would reduce latency for simple existence checks.

Tom B: Yes, a small TTL'd index (trace-metadata) would be cheap. We already store trace-id + root-span timestamp in Clickhouse for alerts; extend that to include storage tier pointer.

Maya L: Question for privacy/compliance: some tenants have retention obligations (e.g., HIPAA). We need exceptions per tenant and a UI to request retention extensions. This ties into quota & billing flows.

Ashwin K: Right — policy needs to be per-tenant overrideable. Proposal: default per-env TTLs, with tenant overrides stored in billing metadata. Enforce via routing at ingestion and retention jobs.

SRE Sam: Operational concern: backfill/rehydrate storms. If many queries hit cold rehydrate at once, could overwhelm pods. We should implement rate-limited rehydrate queue and a circuit-breaker on the API.

Tom B: Also add a fallback model: if rehydrate queue is saturated, return cached summary + pointer to request rehydrate and create a support ticket auto-label. That gives graceful degradation.

Maya L: For rollout, start with a canary: pick 3 non-critical services, enable tenant-aware routing + cold after 7d for dev only. Monitor query latency, support tickets, and cost delta for 2 weeks.

Ashwin K: Timeline: I'll sketch a RFC with config options, migration steps, and observability hooks. Can we get a review from @Maya and @Tom by EOW?

Maya L: Yes. I'll pull current query logs and produce a dashboard with cold-hit latency and rehydrate times.

Tom B: I'll prototype the trace-metadata index and a simple rehydrate queue handler (Python lambda PoC).

Ashwin K: Thanks — adding action items in the RFC. :thumbsup:
